note: A screen, not an audit: questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them. No savings are computed; typical benefits are the cited sources' general wording.

questions.question: What records support this evaporator's defrost applicability, initiation and termination?

evidence.text: equipment EVAP-GROUP reads "EVAP-GROUP Ammonia blast freezer evaporator group"
final element HG-MAIN reads "HG-MAIN Hot gas main valve for defrost" at EVAP-GROUP

data_requests.item: Applicability and actual initiation per named evaporator
where: DCS/PLC configuration: permitted current defrost configuration: target coil/unit, initiation and fallback mode, enabled/disabled state and revision
site records: existing source-owner or supplier records establishing whether defrost applies to this unit and which indications actually initiate it
data_requests.how: Keep timer/demand labels and DP readings as candidates. An indication, termination sensor or unit name does not prove active demand initiation; do not borrow another evaporator's control basis.

where: site records: approved existing frost/coil-pressure and defrost-event records, initiation reason, duration, termination and coincident conditions
maintenance records: relevant recorded inspection or sensor/function checks and their dates
data_requests.how: Separate evidence of need from initiation and termination. Retain quantity/location/units/time and missing history explicitly; no pressure threshold, event count or universal observation duration is supplied.

data_requests.item: Affected room/product constraints and review route
where: historian or DCS trend for HG-MAIN (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
site records: permitted room/product requirements, operating restrictions and existing reviewed defrost basis for the identified unit
the vendor datasheet: applicable unit and control constraints and responsible reviewer
data_requests.how: Use an existing-record fallback when no suitable mapped signal is supplied. Establish relevant effects and constraints through the company review route; no inspection, defrost or setting change is authorized.

questions.decision_rule: Pursue missing applicability, source/function or representative event evidence. A drawn DP instrument or demand label does not settle whether defrost is initiated by actual need. Close only a qualified source investigation; no installed-control acceptance or operating change follows.

typical_benefit.wording: Demand defrost (S25, p. 66): "Evaporators should be defrosted only when necessary, as opposed to on timed schedules where defrosting occurs regardless of need." "Too frequent defrosts." is listed among control strategies that "may compromise system energy efficiency" (S25, p. 59, citing Pearson 2003). No % stated.
source_titles: S25: Brush, Masanet and Worrell, Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for the Dairy Processing Industry: An ENERGY STAR Guide for Energy and Plant Managers (LBNL-6261E, Oct 2011)

questions.limits: S25 printed p.66 discusses need-based defrost; per-unit keep-open collection and accepting an anchor's own description as a candidate are authored software/engineering policy. Neither absence nor presence of a DP/demand/termination label establishes actual use. Applicability, initiation, termination, source revision and operating/product constraints require review. The screen does not infer frost, installed timers, thresholds or permission.
